name: Sessions
summary: Every conversation is saved, so you can resume it, branch it or switch between tasks.
what: Claude Code stores each conversation as a session tied to the project folder you ran it in. You can come back to the last one, pick an older one from a list, give sessions names, or branch a conversation to try a different approach while keeping the original.

impact.title: Pick up where you left off
impact.detail: Continue yesterday's work, even after closing the terminal or clearing the screen.

impact.title: Try ideas safely
impact.detail: Branch a conversation to explore another approach without losing the first one.

impact.title: Find parallel work
impact.detail: Named sessions make it easy to tell several tasks apart.

howItWorks: Run claude --continue to reopen the most recent session in this folder.
Run claude --resume, or /resume inside a session, to pick from a searchable list.
Use /rename or claude -n <name> to name a session.
Use /branch to fork the current conversation into a new session.
Old sessions are cleaned up after 30 days by default (cleanupPeriodDays).

events.note: First changelog mention: claude --continue and claude --resume.
